item.content:encoded:
Necropost, but eh.

Imagine the discussion that went on behind the scenes where Article XII was first proposed. Part of me wants to think that it was proposed as a cold and emotionless response to not having a readily available candidate for 204-1 imprint. While there are people in the Foundation that aren't soulless assholes, there are those that would not consider Article XII as purposefully creating a victim, but rather "preparing a suitable candidate".

I can only guess that there are a lot of very broken people that are continuing to function inside the Foundation by creating pretty harsh barriers between what they're doing and whatever remains of their fragile psyche. The scenario that comes to mind here was that Article XII was proposed in a rather clinical manner by a mentally scarred researcher, then kicked up the chain by horrified supervisors/administrators desperately trying to pass the buck on proposing that someone actually toss a child to a known predator.

Eventually it landed on someone's desk that took a long, hard look at it, and realized that while there could be a scenario in which they'd have to manufacture a victim, it would be highly unlikely that the Foundation would be unable to find a suitable candidate that wasn't "created naturally."

On a related note, I fucking hate that "created naturally" is a thing.

To date, Article XII has not been enacted in any form.

That sells it for me. The Foundation has prepared for the utterly terrible thing they feel they may have to do but haven't actually done it and clearly really, really don't want to. Combined with the fact that they let the kid's go if they think they can this properly makes the "cold, not cruel" thing better than if they were abusing kids regularly to make the process simpler.
